relatedSnapshot.title: Stop one Outlook inbox from retrying forever on a permanently deleted email
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

One connected Outlook inbox has been stuck since last night in an endless retry loop and hasn't synced any new mail since. The cause is a single deleted email that Microsoft answers about in a way our sync doesn't expect, so it fails and immediately tries again, burning background-job time all day.

## Problem

When our Outlook sync notices an email has left a synced folder, it asks Microsoft whether that email simply moved to another synced folder or was actually deleted, before removing it from the CRM. For most deleted emails Microsoft plainly says "this doesn't exist anymore." For this particular email, Microsoft instead answers "access denied, wrong store ID" - a rarer response it sometimes gives for emails that were permanently purged. Our code doesn't recognize that answer as "the email is gone," so it treats it as an unexpected failure, retries several times over a few hours, gives up, and then starts over from scratch on the next sync trigger - forever, for that one inbox.

## Proposed fix

Teach the Outlook sync to also recognize this specific "access denied, wrong store ID" response as meaning the email is gone, the same way it already recognizes a plain "not found" response. Once recognized, sync treats the email as removed and moves on normally, and the affected inbox heals itself on its next sync run with no manual cleanup needed.

## What's included

* Recognizing this specific Microsoft Graph error shape (403 with this exact message) as "item no longer exists," alongside the existing "not found" (404) handling, in the two Outlook message-lookup helpers that can hit it.
* Not included: broader changes to Outlook sync retry behavior, concurrency, or reconnect handling - those are working as intended, and this is a narrow, one-error-shape fix.

## How it should work

* When Microsoft answers with this error while checking a deleted email's current location, sync treats it exactly like "not found": the email is not present in any synced folder, so it gets removed from the CRM (if it was ever imported) and the sync cursor advances normally.
* No change to how genuine access or credential problems are handled - those still stop sync and mark the account for reconnect.

## Who can do what

Not applicable: internal background sync behavior, no user-facing permissions change.

## What the user sees

No visible UI change. The practical effect: once deployed, the affected customer's Outlook inbox starts syncing new mail again on its next scheduled check, with no action needed from them or from us.

## Done when

* The two Outlook Graph message-lookup helpers treat this specific "access denied, wrong store ID" response the same as a "not found" response.
* The account behind ACQUISITY-558 completes a sync run successfully instead of failing.
* Automated tests cover this error shape.

## Open questions

None: all required decisions are settled.

## Expected outcome

Outlook sync stops retrying on permanently deleted emails that Microsoft reports this way, the currently stuck inbox recovers on its own, and background-job usage from this runaway loop stops.

## Implementation context

* Sentry issue: ACQUISITY-558 - 8K+ events over 20 hours, still escalating.
* Failing account: `calendarAccountId` `<uuid>`.
* Failing Graph call (from Sentry breadcrumbs): `GET /me/messages/{id}?$select=id,parentFolderId` returns HTTP 403, body "Access is denied. Check credentials and try again., The store ID provided isn't an ID of an item."
* Code to change: `apps/web/lib/integrations/email/outlook-api-client.ts` (`fetchOutlookMessage`, `fetchOutlookMessageParentFolderId`); add the classifier alongside `isOutlookSyncStateNotFoundError` in `apps/web/lib/integrations/email/outlook-graph-error.ts`.
* Confirmed not caused by the most recent Outlook PR (ENG-13963, merged 2026-09-21) - that PR left this code path byte-for-byte unchanged. The 404-only handling dates back to ENG-13962 (2026-09-19), when this sync path was first written.

relatedSnapshot.title: Inbox sync follow-ups
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Keep useful later inbox-sync controls and edge cases together without delaying reliable Gmail and Microsoft sync.

## Problem

Long-history import, manual repair, shared mailboxes and automatic record creation are useful, but none is required for the normal background-sync outcome.

## Proposed fix

Use this as the Backlog master. Promote only one independently useful outcome at a time after real usage shows it is needed.

## What's included

* Longer or configurable import history.
* Manual resync and detailed diagnostics.
* Automatic Person creation.
* Shared mailbox and alias controls.
* Ambiguous matching review tools.
* Individual conversation repair.
* Broader attachment ingestion.

## How it should work

Nothing here blocks safe workspace binding, provider sync, known-record matching or durable sent-email recovery unless live evidence proves the normal flow cannot work without it.

## Who can do what

Product selects the next outcome. Engineers can record findings here without starting them or changing the current blocker graph.

## What the user sees

Not applicable until a child is selected.

## Done when

- [ ] Later work has one Backlog home.
- [ ] No child blocks the current release by default.
- [ ] Every promoted child has one user outcome and real evidence.

## Open questions

Which control is actually needed after design-partner use? Recommended default: measure sync failures and support burden first.

## Expected outcome

Edge cases remain visible without expanding the current release.

## Implementation context

Promotion rules and deferred technical families are in AI context.md.

## Twenty reference for later controls

Use Twenty CRM as a product and architecture reference. Verify the current source when implementation starts. Learn from its sync boundaries, state machines and user experience, then reimplement the behaviour in Acquisity's Next.js, tRPC, Drizzle and Inngest stack.

Do not copy Twenty application code verbatim or introduce a dependency on Twenty-hosted services. Twenty's core application is AGPL-licensed, so this ticket is about learning from the design and creating an Acquisity-native implementation.

Twenty is especially useful when deciding which later control deserves a child ticket: selected sync folders, per-mailbox visibility or redaction, automatic contact-creation policy, shared mailboxes and aliases, manual resync and diagnostics, provider-deletion repair, and broader attachment ingestion. Do not copy these into the first release by default. Promote one outcome only when design-partner usage or support evidence shows the simple automatic flow is insufficient.

relatedSnapshot.title: Failed to sync changes (AI-CLIENTS-1VV)
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Sentry

* Issue: AI-CLIENTS-1VV
* Title: Error: Failed to sync changes
* Culprit: `inngest:calendar.process-webhook`
* Occurrences: ~18,686
* Users impacted: 1
* First seen: 2025-12-12 / Last seen: 2026-06-16 (ongoing)
* Environment: production, release main

## Root cause (best effort)

Throwing site: `apps/web/lib/integrations/calendar/google-calendar-webhook-service.ts:114` (`handleWebhookError`), rethrown from `syncChanges` at line 541.

Call path: `inngest/functions/calendar/process-webhook.ts:94` -> `lib/scheduling/services/calendar-sync-service.ts:203` (`processCalendarChanges`) -> `GoogleCalendarWebhookService.syncChanges` -> `handleWebhookError`.

`handleWebhookError` already special-cases 400/401/auth (`invalid_grant`, token expired/revoked, unauthorized, bad request) into a "reconnect your Name 6 Calendar" error, and `syncChanges` handles 410 (invalid sync token) by performing a full re-sync. The remaining `throw new GoogleCalendarWebhookError("Failed to ${action}")` is a generic catch-all that **discards the original Name 6 API error code/message**, so the underlying cause is not visible in the Sentry event. The high volume (~18.7k events) concentrated on a **single user** points to one calendar account stuck in a persistent failure loop, re-triggered on every `calendar/webhook.received` rather than a broad code regression.

## Why this is not yet code-fixable

* The actual upstream error code/category is swallowed by the generic rethrow; we cannot deterministically reproduce or classify it from the current stack.
* This exact symptom has recurred and been re-triaged multiple times without a durable code fix: ENG-3811 (Canceled, linked in Sentry), ENG-8043 / ENG-8053 (Canceled), ENG-3306 (Done). The persistent single-user, high-count pattern suggests a per-account / upstream condition rather than a clean defect.

## Suggested next step for a human

Improve observability before attempting a fix: include the original Name 6 API `error.code` and message in the `GoogleCalendarWebhookError` and Sentry context (without leaking PII), and identify the single affected account so it can be inspected (likely a stale channel, deleted calendar, or persistent upstream condition). Then decide whether to suppress/expire the dead webhook channel.

Related existing tickets: ENG-3811, ENG-3306, ENG-8043, ENG-8053.

relatedSnapshot.title: ColdMailReseller pre-warmed inboxes stuck in Error: reconnect sends mailboxId=undefined ("Mailbox not found")
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Pre-warmed mailboxes provisioned through ColdMailReseller get stuck in an Error state and cannot send, because no reconnect path resolves a mailbox id the provider will accept.

## Problem

When a ColdMailReseller pre-warmed inbox disconnects or needs reconnecting, the account-error reconnect flow fires with `mailboxId: providerId ?? undefined`. These inboxes have `mail_inbox.provider_id = NULL`, so the provider receives `mailboxId=undefined` and the OAuth connect returns "Mailbox not found", leaving the inbox permanently in Error.

## Root cause

`apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/campaign/workspaces/process-account-error-reconnect.ts` invokes `processConnectOAuth` with `mailboxId: inboxLookup.providerId ?? undefined`. `processConnectOAuth` (`process-connect-oauth.ts`, `connect-mailbox-oauth` step) forwards that `mailboxId` to ColdMailReseller `POST /mailboxes/oauth` via `apps/web/lib/mail/providers/coldmailreseller/client.ts#connectMailboxOAuth`, which rejects it with "Mailbox not found". The inboxes have `mail_inbox.provider_id = NULL`, so the id is never resolved. The reconcile cron (`reconcile-domain-orders-cron.ts`) already looks up the mailbox from ColdMailReseller and passes `mailbox.id` correctly, so the resolution pattern exists.

The failing invariant is one gap across every entry point: no reconnect path resolves the mailbox id from ColdMailReseller before calling the provider. The webhook path forwards the stored `mail_inbox.provider_id`; the customer Reconnect action (`email-accounts.ts`, `triggerOAuthReconnect`) and the admin reconnect (`admin-domain-orders.ts`) both send `mailboxId: undefined`; `processConnectOAuth` never re-resolves. An inbox carrying a named but no-longer-valid id fails identically to one with a NULL id, which is why both counts below sit in this one class.

## Blast radius

5,762 inboxes across 444 organizations carry a `connection_error` containing "Mailbox not found" (query: `SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT organization_id) FROM mail_inbox WHERE connection_error ILIKE '%Mailbox not found%'`, counted 2026-09-24: 5,762 inboxes / 444 organizations, and 7,071 reconnect sessions across 461 organizations failed the same way in the 30 days to 2026-09-24; was 5,763 / 445 on 2026-09-23, 5,660 / 439 on 2026-09-22, 4,364 / 323 on 2026-09-10 and 294 / 39 on 2026-08-28). None of the 5,762 is connected now. 2,391 of them carry the exact `mailboxId=undefined` signature (and all of those have `provider_id IS NULL`); the larger 3,371 carry a named mailbox id and fail the same way. Named-id rows arrive in platform waves (2026-09-04 to 09-06 roughly 2,118 rows across 95+ organizations; 2026-09-19 to 09-20 roughly 1,148 rows across 103 organizations), so the shape is systematic rather than org-specific. A further 2,872 connected pre-warmed inboxes across 228 organizations sit at `provider_id IS NULL` and would fail the same way on their next reconnect.

## Proposed fix

Resolve the provider mailbox id before reconnecting: look up the mailbox from ColdMailReseller (as the reconcile cron already does) instead of passing `provider_id` or `undefined`, and backfill `provider_id` for the affected inboxes so they reconnect successfully.

## Done when

* No reconnect path hands ColdMailReseller an unresolved id: the webhook path stops forwarding the stored `provider_id` unresolved, the customer Reconnect and admin reconnect stop sending `undefined`, and both shapes (NULL `provider_id` and stale named id) reconnect successfully.
* The stuck inboxes are recovered or re-provisioned and resume sending.
* Provider accounts with no local `mail_inbox` row are covered too: Reconnect refuses them outright (`email-accounts.ts#triggerOAuthReconnect` throws PRECONDITION_FAILED "Only managed inboxes can be reconnected.") while their inbox entitlements are still consumed, so the backfill and re-provision step must create or link the missing rows, not only repair a NULL or stale `provider_id`.

## Reports

* ENG-13156
* ENG-13255
* ENG-13511
* ENG-14104
* ENG-14131
* ENG-14197 Customer report: all 15 pre-warmed inboxes stuck in Error; Reconnect returns Mailbox not found; campaigns cannot send
* ENG-14201 Customer report: 15 of 36 pre-warmed inboxes stuck in Error; Reconnect returns Mailbox not found and never clears the inbox

relatedSnapshot.title: Fix 5 bugs identified in automated code review (2026-03-06)
relatedSnapshot.description:
Five bugs found during automated review of commits landed in the last 24 hours.

## Bugs fixed

**1. Silent failures in batch token refresh** (`lib/inngest/functions/integrations/refresh-email-tokens-cron.ts`)
The first `processBatch` call (marking accounts without refresh tokens as invalid) returned `PromiseSettledResult[]` that was immediately discarded. Any unexpected promise rejections were never logged or sent to Sentry. Fixed by capturing the results and logging rejections.

**2. Unbounded duplicate offset in workflow builder** (`components/workflows/builder/workflow-context-menu.tsx`)
`duplicateOffsetRef` accumulated by 24px on every duplicate action for the lifetime of the component. After \~40 duplications nodes would be placed far off-screen. Fixed by resetting the offset to 24 whenever the context menu closes.

**3. Unsaveable "Not set" selection in campaign type selector** (`components/campaigns/detail/tabs/options/campaign-type-selector-card.tsx`)
Selecting "Not set" set `emailScriptsMethod = null` and showed the Save button, but the button was `disabled` when `!emailScriptsMethod` — a broken UX with no explanation. The `handleSave` null guard was also unreachable dead code. Fixed by hiding the Save button when the selected value is null (the API cannot clear the field).

**4. Type-unsafe fallback in campaign imports** (`lib/inngest/functions/campaign/process-campaign-imports.ts`)
`c.raw ?? c` substituted the normalized `WithRaw<NormCampaign>` object when `raw` was absent, then cast it to `Campaign[]`. Downstream code expecting raw provider fields would receive wrong field names silently. Reverted to the original filter-out-undefined behaviour.

**5. Workshop campaign type bypassing DB settings** (`lib/ai-sdr-v2/workflow/helpers/get-call-type.ts`)
The `workshop` branch returned before the `try` block, so it never read `aiSdrSettings` from the database. Unlike `podcast` and `interview`, the workshop call type was hardcoded and could not be configured via AI SDR settings. Moved inside the `try` block and added to the `catch` fallback.

## Related

* ENG-6177 (duplicate step — Workflows project)
* ENG-5915 (AI Audit / workshop — AI SDR project)

- [ ] Verified aliases and delegated sending.

Use the existing follow-up and matching scope before creating duplicates. Later controls must not block the basic sync release through a blanket dependency.

Provider archive changes should also clear the Acquisity action item. Read, Done and delete are separate actions; another recipient's work must not be cleared.

The initial target is Gmail/Microsoft. Custom IMAP/SMTP, bulk email, tracking and snippets require separate scope decisions. No trial or Close cutover is scheduled by this ticket.

relatedSnapshot.title: Keep connected inboxes synced with CRM
relatedSnapshot.description:
**Closed 25 Sep 2026. The Gmail half is complete: ENG-12668, ENG-12256, ENG-12690, ENG-12669 and ENG-12569 are all Done. Microsoft 365 sync continues in ENG-12972. Live QA for both providers is tracked in the completion checklist of ENG-13574. The live QA and PostHog activation boxes below were not re-checked when this was closed.**

## Overview

Make connected Gmail and Microsoft 365 inboxes a reliable source of CRM conversations.

Once a mailbox is connected to a workspace, recent and new sales emails should appear automatically. Users should not need to open a tab, manually refresh or repair missing history.

## Problem

CRM can fetch and save known provider threads, but it does not continuously sync an entire mailbox. Mailbox accounts are user-scoped rather than explicitly bound to workspaces, and opening the Emails tab can trigger provider searches and database writes.

## Proposed fix

Create one clear pipeline:

1. Bind a mailbox to exactly one workspace.
2. Import a bounded recent Inbox and Sent window.
3. Keep Gmail and Microsoft updated in the background.
4. Save idempotently.
5. Link messages to records we already know.
6. Make confirmed sent email durable.
7. Show simple sync health.

## What's included

* Connect one mailbox to the right workspace.
* Sync rep inboxes automatically.
  * Gmail.
  * Microsoft 365.
* Stop the Emails tab importing provider data.
* Link synced emails to known CRM records.
* Never lose a sent email.

Later controls and unusual cases belong in Inbox sync follow-ups.

## Execution order

### Wave 1: safe workspace binding

1. Connect one mailbox to the right workspace.

### Wave 2: provider sync

2. Gmail sync.
3. Microsoft 365 sync.

Both providers are blocked by the workspace binding. They may overlap after the shared state contract is settled, but Gmail remains the preferred first pickup.

### Wave 3: remove old imports and enrich saved messages

4. Stop the Emails tab importing provider data.
5. Link synced emails to known CRM records.
6. Never lose a sent email.

The matching and sent-email tickets may overlap once provider sync is complete.

### Wave 4: evidence-led controls

7. Inbox sync follow-ups remains Backlog work. Promote one independently useful control only after live usage shows it is needed. It does not block the reliable default sync.

## How it should work

* Every job resolves one active workspace binding.
* Initial import and notifications are idempotent.
* Cursors advance only after messages are saved.
* Disconnect prevents further writes before provider cleanup.
* Old-generation jobs stop safely.
* Missing or delayed sync is visible.
* Page views read CRM data only.
* Ambiguous matching never guesses.

## Who can do what

Users connect only their own mailbox into a workspace they belong to. Every background job, read and write enforces the stored workspace binding and current access.

## What the user sees

Existing account settings show Setting up, Syncing, Up to date, Delayed, Reconnect required or Disconnected. CRM records receive email history automatically.

## Done when

- [ ] A connected mailbox belongs to one workspace.
- [ ] Recent Inbox and Sent conversations import automatically.
- [ ] New Gmail and Microsoft messages arrive without a page load.
- [ ] Replay and duplicate notifications create one CRM message.
- [ ] Disconnect prevents further writes.
- [ ] Known People are linked deterministically.
- [ ] Confirmed sent email eventually appears after temporary failure.
- [ ] Live Gmail and Microsoft QA passes.
- [ ] Activation events are verified in PostHog.

## Open questions

Confirm the first-import history window. Recommended default: 90 days.

## Expected outcome

Connected inboxes behave like dependable CRM infrastructure instead of page-triggered provider imports.

## Twenty reference

Use Twenty CRM as a product and architecture reference. Verify the current source when implementation starts. Learn from its sync boundaries, state machines and user experience, then reimplement the behaviour in Acquisity's Next.js, tRPC, Drizzle and Inngest stack.

Do not copy Twenty application code verbatim or introduce a dependency on Twenty-hosted services. Twenty's core application is AGPL-licensed, so this ticket is about learning from the design and creating an Acquisity-native implementation.

Specifically study how Twenty separates first import from continuous sync, treats provider notifications as wake-up signals, persists provider checkpoints only after successful writes, recovers stale cursors, processes provider deletions, and associates message participants before CRM matching. Folder selection, per-mailbox visibility and automatic contact creation are useful later controls, but remain in ENG-12970 so the first release stays simple.

relatedSnapshot.title: Name 8 Sync fails silently because its job can't read issues
relatedSnapshot.description:
## What's happening

The Name 8 Sync job in CI finds the PR's ticket, then stops with `Sync error: "Resource not accessible by integration ... issues#get-an-issue"` and still reports success. So it never checks CI status and never posts the preview deployment comment to Name 8.

## What should happen

Name 8 Sync reads the PR's labels, checks CI, and posts the deployment comment to the ticket.

## Who it hits and how bad

Every PR with a preview. In 9 of 9 sampled runs that executed (the last 12 of 85 PR runs, 15 Oct 2026), it failed this way. Nobody notices, because the job shows green.

## How to see it

Open the Name 8 Sync job log on any recent PR CI run. After "Found Name 8 ticket", the next line is the 403 `Sync error`.

## What we know so far

The `linear-sync` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` has `pull-requests: write`, `contents: read`, `checks: read` and `statuses: read`, but no `issues: read`. `getCurrentStatusLabels` in `.github/scripts/linear-sync.ts` calls the issues API. Adding `issues: read` is likely the whole fix, but nobody has tested it yet.

## Done when

- [ ] On a PR run, the Name 8 Sync log shows no `Sync error`, and the ticket gets the preview deployment comment.
- [ ] The job fails, not passes, when the sync errors.

relatedSnapshot.title: Inbox sync corrections
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Connected Gmail should bring a rep's conversations with CRM contacts into the CRM, and nothing else. This master corrects the first Gmail sync release so it stops saving unrelated mail, removes what was already imported, finds a new contact's history in every rep's inbox, and shows one conversation when several reps received the same email.

## Problem

The first Gmail import and live sync save every Inbox and Sent email from the last 90 days, whether or not anyone on it is in the CRM. Since 16 September 2026 that added about 1.84 million messages (about 29 GB) to production, and 98% of them are not linked to any contact. Most are newsletters and personal mail. The database storage alert on 17 September came from this.

The design came from Keep connected inboxes synced with CRM and Link synced emails to CRM records we already know, which stored all mail first and matched later. We are changing that to Close's model: only mail involving CRM contacts is stored, and a new contact's past mail is found on demand.

## What's included

* Stop saving Gmail mail that does not involve a CRM contact, and keep a small address index so later contacts can still find their history.
* Delete the Gmail mail imported before the new rule.
* Find a new contact's past emails in every rep's connected inbox.
* Merge copies of the same email received by several reps into one conversation.

Related, not in this master: Share all communications on records (Close visibility model) owns team visibility, the sync blocklist and internal-address exclusion. Microsoft sync is not changed here.

## Execution order

Use the lowest-numbered eligible ticket first. Tickets explicitly grouped as parallel may start together when there is capacity, but they still keep the priority order below. Waves show the earliest dependency unlock, not a barrier: start a later-wave ticket as soon as its own blockers are complete.

### Wave 1: can start now

Parallel: none.

1. Stop saving Gmail mail that does not involve a CRM contact: only contact-matched mail is stored, with an address index and a kill switch.

### Wave 2: starts when ticket 1 is complete

Parallel: Delete the Gmail mail imported before the contact-match rule with either Find a new contact's past emails in every rep's inbox or Show one conversation when several reps got the same email. Tickets 3 and 4 both change how emails are saved, so run them one after the other.

2. Delete the Gmail mail imported before the contact-match rule: blocked by ticket 1.
3. Find a new contact's past emails in every rep's inbox: blocked by ticket 1.
4. Show one conversation when several reps got the same email: blocked by ticket 1.

Cross-wave overlap: None.

## Done when

- [ ] Gmail import and live sync store only threads that involve a CRM contact or company.
- [ ] Mail imported before the rule is deleted and the space is reused.
- [ ] Adding a contact brings in their past emails from every rep's connected inbox.
- [ ] The same email received by several reps shows as one conversation.

relatedSnapshot.title: Subscription cancellation test fails on a timestamp race, not a real bug
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

One unit test in the subscription cancellation safety suite fails on roughly four in ten runs. The code it tests is correct. The test checks the lease token on the wrong part of the database update, so it only passes when two timestamps happen to land in the same millisecond.

## Problem

The test named "uses the reservation token to fence provider-result persistence" fails on about 4 of 10 runs locally and in CI. It turned the Unit Tests job on main red twice on 14 September with no related code change. Every failure shows the same thing: the completion timestamp is 1 to 8 ms later than the reservation timestamp. Because it sits among 35,000 unit tests, every push carries a real chance of a red Unit Tests job that has nothing to do with the change.

## Proposed fix

Make the test assert what its name says: that the update which records the provider result is fenced on the reservation token in its WHERE condition. Leave the implementation alone.

## What's included

Included: the one assertion in that test.

Not included: any change to the cancellation code, the lease and fencing behaviour, or the other tests in the same file.

## How it should work

The finalizing update writes a fresh "last synced" time and refuses to touch a row whose lease token no longer matches. The test proves the second half by inspecting the WHERE conditions the update was called with, so it passes regardless of how long the flow took.

## Who can do what

Not applicable: test-only change.

## What the user sees

Not applicable: test-only change.

## Done when

* The test passes on 20 consecutive local runs.
* The assertion reads the reservation token from the WHERE conditions of the finalizing update, not from its SET payload.
* The Unit Tests job on main no longer fails on this test.
* The implementation file is untouched.

## Open questions

None: all required decisions are settled.

## Expected outcome

A red Unit Tests job on main means a real failure again.

## Implementation context

The test is at subscription-cancellation-safety.test.ts line 1021. The code it exercises is `finalizeAutomaticRemovalLease` and `automaticLeaseWhere` in subscription-cancellation-safety.ts. Both arrived with Acquisity/Acquisity#6226 for ENG-10751. Latest failing run: Unit Tests on main, 2026-09-14.

relatedSnapshot.title: CMR subscription snapshot sync fails on subscriptions without a domain
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

The CMR subscription snapshot sync failed on **every** full audit because ColdMailReseller returned a subscription with no `domain` (`data.subscriptions[22].domain`). Zod rejected the whole page, so `cmr_subscription_snapshot` stayed empty and findings had no CMR subscription status, period end or auto-renew.

One malformed row from the provider was enough to take out the entire snapshot, and the failure was silent from the audit's point of view — it just produced findings with missing subscription state.

## Root cause

The subscriptions list response schema required `domain` to be a non-null string, and validation ran over the whole page rather than per row, so a single domainless subscription failed the batch.

## Solution

* Accept a missing/null `domain` in the subscriptions **list response**; `Subscription.domain` stays a required string downstream, so nothing further down has to handle the looser shape.
* Skip domainless (or blank) subscriptions in `fetchSubscriptionsPage` and log `cmr_subscriptions_without_domain` with the page and subscription IDs.
* The empty-page guard in `listAllSubscriptions` counts **raw provider rows**, so a page consisting only of domainless subscriptions doesn't abort the walk and later pages are still collected.

## Impact

* **Admin-facing:** the weekly CMR billing audit has been running without any subscription state. Anything that depends on `cmr_subscription_snapshot` — `overcharged` detection, "billing ends <date>" notes, pending-cancellation badges — was degraded.
* **Blast radius:** affects every full (unscoped) audit run, not a subset.

## Testing

* New client tests for missing / null / blank domains, and for a page containing only domainless subscriptions.
* `client.test.ts` and `cmr-domain-audit.test.ts` pass; typecheck passes.

## Verification after deploy

Run an unscoped "Run audit now" and confirm `cmr_subscription_snapshot` is populated. Check the logs for `cmr_subscriptions_without_domain` to see how many rows CMR is actually sending domainless.

## Notes

3 files, +61/-9. Fixes the sync introduced in Acquisity/Acquisity#6591. Part of the CMR domain audit series.

relatedSnapshot.title: Run CI Name 8 Sync from trusted code and fail on sync errors
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

The `linear-sync` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` fails systemically on pull-request runs but remains green.

A read-only audit of PR #5663 run `29591643738` found:

* The job checks out the pull-request head and executes that branch's `.github/scripts/linear-sync.ts`.
* The script calls GitHub's issue endpoint to read and reconcile PR status labels.
* The job has `pull-requests: write`, `contents: read`, `checks: read`, and `statuses: read`, but no `issues` permission.
* GitHub returns `403 Resource not accessible by integration`.
* The script records `success=false` but does not fail the step, so CI stays green and skips the expected deployment comment.
* Ten out of ten sampled recent pull-request CI runs across unrelated branches contain the same 403.

The canonical `.github/workflows/linear-sync.yml` route already has `issues: write` and successfully handles PR events.

This is separate from ENG-11759, which changes Name 8 ticket-reference resolver parity and does not own CI token permissions, trusted workflow execution, or fail-open reporting.

## Security boundary

Do not fix this by only adding `issues: write` while continuing to run privileged synchronization code from the pull-request head. The job combines a Name 8 secret with a GitHub write-capable token, so executable sync code must come from a trusted default-branch source.

## Acceptance criteria

* The privileged CI Name 8 Sync path executes trusted default-branch workflow or script code rather than the pull-request head's implementation.
* The sync job has the minimum required `issues: write` permission because it reads and reconciles labels.
* Unexpected GitHub API, Name 8 API, or synchronization failures fail the CI step and job.
* Expected no-op outcomes remain successful and are reported distinctly from failures.
* Workflow contract coverage verifies the trusted-code boundary and required permission set.
* Focused tests verify failure propagation from the sync result to the CI process exit or action failure.
* Coverage demonstrates that pull-request code cannot replace the privileged sync implementation.
* Existing successful label reconciliation and deployment-comment behavior remains intact.

## Out of scope

* Changing ENG-11759's resolver-parity implementation.
* Broadening permissions outside the Name 8 Sync job.
* Executing or merging the implementation as part of ticket creation.

relatedSnapshot.title: Master: Resuming AI SDR does not re-run it, so the response-timeout monitor re-escalates the thread
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When an operator returns an AI SDR thread to automation - Resume AI SDR after an escalation, dismissing an escalation back to automated, or re-enabling the AI SDR toggle - the AI SDR never processes the prospect reply that is still waiting. The response-timeout monitor escalates the thread again within about 15 minutes, it reads as AI SDR Disabled / Needs Attention again, and prospects stay unanswered for days. The operator cannot hand a conversation back to the AI SDR.

## Problem

From the operator's side: they review an escalated thread, resolve the reason it escalated, resume the AI SDR, and it is escalated again within one monitor tick with no AI SDR attempt. The same thread loops however often it is resumed, which is reported by customers as the AI SDR switching itself off.

## Root cause

`resumeFromEscalation` and `dismissEscalation` in `apps/web/trpc/routers/ai-sdr.ts` (about lines 1588 and 1516) and the re-enable toggle (about line 860) end at `updateControlLevel` plus `escalationDismissedAt`. None of them emits `ai-sdr-v2/message.received`, the only trigger of `aiSdrV2Workflow` (`apps/web/lib/ai-sdr-v2/workflow/workflow.ts`), so the pending prospect reply is never processed.

`monitor-ai-sdr-response-timeout.ts` (`check-for-timeouts`, cron `*/15 * * * *`) then escalates any `controlLevel='automated'` thread whose newest recorded message is an inbound reply older than 2 hours and which has never booked, and it never reads `escalation_dismissed_at`. The resume is therefore undone at the next tick.

Scope note for the fix: ENG-8377 ("AI SDR: Allow automation to resume after escalation", Done) defines Resume as making "the next inbound prospect reply" pass the eligibility check, so not re-running the AI SDR for the pending reply was the shipped intent. That points at the monitor side (honour the resume - the newest resume timestamp in `control_level_history` or `escalation_dismissed_at` - or reset the 2-hour clock on resume) unless product decides Resume should also process the pending reply.

## Blast radius

Counted 2026-09-28, 45-day window, all organizations: 2104 resume-then-re-escalation pairs, 1105 distinct threads, 275 distinct organizations, 258 distinct operator users. An independent recount with the same pairing logic returned a slightly higher 2802 pairs / 1208 threads / 280 organizations / 263 users, so the recorded figure is conservative. In every pair measured, zero AI SDR agent executions occur between the resume and the re-escalation.

Query: pairs where a `crm_message_thread.control_level_history` entry `to='automated'` from `'escalated'` or `'human_takeover'` is followed within 2 hours by an entry `to='escalated'` with `updatedBy='monitor-ai-sdr-response-timeout'` (jsonb_array_elements joined on thread_id, `m.ts > r.ts AND m.ts <= r.ts + interval '2 hours'`), left-checked against `agent_executions` in the interval.

Potentially exposed: every thread an operator returns to automated after an escalation.

## Proposed fix

Make the either/or explicit and implement it: a thread returned to automated must not be re-escalated by the response-timeout monitor before the AI SDR has had a chance on it. Either honour the resume when evaluating timeout candidates, or trigger the AI SDR on resume for the pending reply.

## What's included

The monitor/resume decision and its regression test. Related, not included: ENG-14111 (a sent AI SDR reply is never recorded, which the same monitor also turns into an escalation) and ENG-10060 (periodic provider-versus-local thread/message reconciliation).

## Regression seam

`check-for-timeouts` in `apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/monitor-ai-sdr-response-timeout.ts`. Red before: a thread whose control level returned to `automated` with no new inbound is escalated by the monitor at the next tick. Green after: such a thread is not escalated, or, if Resume is redefined, the AI SDR runs for the pending reply. `apps/web/tests/lib/inngest/functions/monitor-ai-sdr-response-timeout-db.test.ts` already exercises the candidate filters against Postgres and is the place to add the resumed-thread case.

## Done when

* A thread returned to automated after an escalation is not re-escalated by the response-timeout monitor before the AI SDR has acted or the resume has been honoured.
* No prospect reply is left unanswered because a resume silently did nothing.
* A regression test proves the behaviour at the named seam.

## Reports

* ENG-14415
